input_policy: Copy pinned segment2.py and templates.py into an isolated directory. Copy the 56 hosted LP2 JPEGs only after checking each against the source capsule's SHA-256, byte count and archive-published SHA-1. Do not copy or modify canonical text, hosted images, or any source checkout output.

preexecution_benchmark.comment: Microbenchmarks of constituent operations on this host, not a runtime guarantee; full segmentation includes crop serialization and template clustering.

control_interpretation: segment2.py and templates.py do not read canonical text; their shape clustering is label-free. Later read.py/diff.py use the canon to name classes and evaluate agreement, so that later percentage is not a wholly independent transcription. Matching output dimensions/counts is a reproducibility check, not proof that individual rune identities or image-glyph judgments are correct.

isolated_input_copy.verification: Each hosted JPEG matched the capsule SHA-256, byte count and archive-published SHA-1 before copying to the isolated data/relikd/p0..p55.jpg names.

segment2.source_comparison: All three aggregate counts match pinned source geometry/shape reports. All 646 page IDs and band indices align with the archived read_lines.json. The original source NPZ digest was unavailable; byte and array identity are not established.

templates.source_comparison: Distinct bitmap and covered-glyph counts match the archived report, but shape-class counts do not. The original source NPZ digest was unavailable.

diagnostics: An isolated copy rerun with OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 produced the same 229 classes and byte-identical templates.npz (11.386 seconds).

A separate diagnostic copy using stable argsort for template-size ordering also produced the same 229 classes and byte-identical templates.npz (5.8 seconds). This does not establish the mismatch cause.
execution.downstream_gate: The historical template-class count was not reproduced. The original downstream read.py and diff.py were subsequently run on the fresh 229-class instrument; their outputs, exact differences, and dependence on canonical text are recorded under downstream_original_routine. The historical artifacts remain unreproduced, but fresh fixed-code runs with pinned new outputs are possible.
execution.independence_limit: The two executed scripts are label-free with respect to canonical transcription. They reproduce geometry dimensions, not rune identities. Later diff.py compares with canon and is not an independent validation of every glyph.

downstream_original_routine.source_copy_check: All four downstream source files were byte-identical to the pinned checkout in the isolated copy. No hosted image, source checkout, or canonical input was changed.
downstream_original_routine.historical_226_status: 226 is a saved templates_report.json count, not a hard-coded trust gate in read.py or diff.py. read.py dynamically retains every class covering at least 100 glyphs, so the fresh 229-class rebuild selects 33 templates rather than the historical 32.
downstream_original_routine.read_line_count_comparison: All 646 line-band page IDs and indices match. Glyph counts differ on 4 bands: band 91/page 8 (25 versus 27), 261/page 22 (104 versus 107), 262/page 22 (43 versus 44), and 635/page 54 (43 versus 45); 642 band glyph counts match.
downstream_original_routine.fresh_in_sample_label_fit: 5011/5229 = 95.831% after fitting 29 class-to-rune assignments on those same equal-count lines; 118 disagreements are emitted among assigned classes. The 218 nonmatches by subtraction include unassigned classes and should not be relabeled as independent transcription errors.
downstream_original_routine.training_provenance: The original diff.py parses LP2 canonical rune text, selects equal-count aligned lines, builds a class-by-rune confusion matrix on those lines, optimizes a one-to-one class assignment using that matrix, then scores those same lines. It does not train on independently solved LP1 text and has no held-out evaluation set; held-out line count is 0.
downstream_original_routine.interpretation: The fixed source code completes on exact recovered JPEGs with a fresh 229-class instrument. Its raw 233 equal-count lines are close to but not identical to the archived 232. This is a fresh fixed-code rerun, not an exact replay of the historical NPZ/read-lines artifacts or an independent verification of rune identities. A source experiment may be rerun with this fresh instrument if it explicitly pins and checks these new outputs; it cannot silently inherit the archived 226-class or 96.93% receipts.
